purpose: Manuscript v26 method coverage: distinguish common scientific procedure from study-specific executed software, source and information regimes.
conclusion: A common evidence-to-generative-law procedure is supported by versioned studies; no single current release was tested across them. Bounded existing analytical-use findings require accurate labeling and existing corrections, not new execution.
common_scientific_invariants: Specify an analytical population, output variables/units and intended subsequent analysis; accept only the information stated for that study.
A scientific author interprets admitted aggregate evidence and chooses an explicit generative law, numerical specification and unresolved completion/transport assumptions.

Most modern studies execute authored programs to produce complete participant-like tables; the program, not the language model, samples rows. Historical literal-row/augmentation studies are separate modes.
Review execution/contracts and scientific source interpretation separately; qualify nonmatching source operations rather than equate unsupported checks with fidelity.
Bind the selected candidate and evaluation plan before the reported reserved reference comparison; repeated seeds sample a law and do not count as new scientific constructions.
Compare the generated tables using fixed analyses, retaining failures, unavailable checks and counterresults. Source fit, target transport and downstream utility remain distinct claims.
noninvariants: Author counts, model identity, autonomy, retrieval access and source packet preparation are not shared constants.
Controllers, schemas, units, row schedules, cell quotas, source operators, estimators and final retention aliases differ.
Optional review/revision support does not mean a scientific revision occurred; nearly all modern retained candidates are initial models.
Source-projection feedback ranges from unavailable or target-row proxy to analytic reviewed uptake to explicit separate source-context execution. These are not interchangeable.
Frozen law identity and common low-level execution hashes do not make different controllers one release.
Reference status ranges from researcher-exposed developmental samples, prospective reference, supplied-source reconstruction to no clinical target read.
Procedural source access and hash commitments are not isolation of the author's general tools or proof of no unlogged/pretraining exposure.

cross_version_evidence.finding: Old main Session demands zero query/download budget and snapshots registry. Open retrieval requires changed adapter; main and evcBuild01 runners cannot be reused unchanged.

Core uses trial then retain/revise then three new final draws; evcBuild01 delivered three initial finals before decision and aliases retained tables. Schemas, units and provider/evaluator definitions also differ.

Compact iron_runner is explicitly not the six-author controller or full signed-off semantic-feedback manifest. The worker contract is common; source-task numerics and lifecycle implementation are study-specific.

Source-replay adapter adds whole-cohort source contexts and projection operations on adaptive v2, but its 24 numerical comparisons remain in an assumption-qualified lane and all strict semantic entries remain unavailable.

recommended_method_text: We studied a common procedure through several frozen implementations: an Agent interpreted the admissible evidence, specified a stochastic generative law and its unresolved assumptions, and produced tables for prespecified analyses. Retrieval access, source-check operators, review and revision schedules, and execution controllers were study-specific and are reported separately. Most modern studies sampled records from Agent-authored programs; historical literal-row and augmentation studies used different input and generation modes. Newer adaptive and source-context interfaces were exercised in separate developmental or source-only studies and were not retrospectively used in the earlier experiments.

verification_note: Only selected aggregate reports, metadata manifests and code files were hashed; no clinical or generated tables were opened. Full execution-inventory verification is retained in the original audits and was not rerun.
